parsed.gloss: There was nothing; there was God. If there had been no God, there would have been no God. I was put together by being; what else would I be?
parsed.literal: If there were nothing, there would be God; if there were not this, there would be that. Had there been no being, I would have been something else.
parsed.poetic: When all is said and done, there's only God. If there had been no Being, what would I have been? (Ghalib)
notes: The 'nothing' of the first line refers to the world as we know it; the 'God' is the Absolute, which is always there. The 'this' and 'that' are the opposites in the duality of existence. 'Being' translates 'hun' (to be), which means both 'existence' and 'I am', so Ghalib refers to himself as a product of his own being. In the last line, 'what would I have been?' is an open question; it's not clear what he was going to say next.
